Visits for 99215 are also heavily weighted toward 99214, which is worth noting as a possible general shift upward. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims are the main concern: several carry only minor acute or follow-up diagnoses, such as a follow-up exam (C0216557), an upper respiratory infection (C0217111) and a rash (C0217298), which would not usually support high-complexity decision-making. The sampled high-complexity 99215s (for example C0216023 and C0216403) look clinically plausible. Documentation does not settle the question, since only two documented 99215 claims exist (both supported) and the single no-lab data-review note is weak evidence at most. The modest peer z-score adds further ambiguity. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for low-complexity 99215 claims like those listed, to check whether documented MDM and time actually support the billed level."}
